proof.criterion: Acceptance 1 and 2a: a rewatch that fails once after a reconnect is retried, the listener ends with a live watch and current caches, and no ERROR is logged for a retry that later succeeds.
proof.surface: The built envoy-listener binary (go build -o $TMPDIR/smoke/envoy-listener ./cmd/listener) against a real nats-server v2.10.29 with JetStream, restarted under it; /healthz and GET /v1/interests/ over HTTP.
proof.command: bash $TMPDIR/smoke/smoke.sh, steps 2 and 3: start the server and the listener, curl /healthz, stop and start nats-server, curl /healthz, POST /v1/interests/subscribe, GET /v1/interests/, then count ERROR lines in the listener's log.
proof.observed: /healthz 200 {"status":"healthy"} at start and again after the restart; the interest written after the restart was served by GET /v1/interests/; the log held 'INFO envoy nats reconnected name=envoy url=nats://127.0.0.1:14222' and 0 ERROR lines.

proof.criterion: Acceptance 2b: a rewatch still failing after the stated bound (bus.RepairGrace, one minute, measured from the connection event) is reported on the listener's health, not only logged.
proof.surface: The same built envoy-listener binary and real nats-server; the server restarted with a configuration that denies only $JS.API.CONSUMER.CREATE.KV_envoy_interests/.roles/.sessions, so STREAM.INFO, the pings and the durable keep working while every KV watch creation fails; /healthz over HTTP.
proof.command: bash $TMPDIR/smoke/smoke.sh, steps 4 and 5: restart under the deny configuration, poll /healthz, read the listener's WARN and ERROR lines, then restart under the allow configuration and poll /healthz again.
proof.observed: Inside the grace: WARN 'envoy nats reconnect hook failed; it is retried ... stall_ms=20007' and 'stall_ms=40015' while /healthz stayed 200 healthy. Past the grace: ERROR 'envoy nats reconnect hooks have not succeeded ... stall_ms=61022' and /healthz 503 {"status":"unhealthy","error":"KV watch rebuild unavailable: rewatch interest cache: watch interest registry KV bucket: context deadline exceeded\nrewatch session cache: watch session registry KV bucket: context deadline exceeded (no rebuild has succeeded for 1m0s)"}. With the deny lifted, the next recovery repaired the caches, /healthz returned to 200 healthy, and an interest written then was served.
proof.negativeControl: The same scenario as a Go test at the base 88840d35, with a real 75 s wait in place of the clock: go test ./cmd/listener/ -run TestBaseHealthzAnswersAHookStallPastAMinute -> FAIL, '/healthz 75 s into a rebuild that never succeeded = 200 map[... status:healthy], want 503 unhealthy'. The base answers healthy however long the rebuild has failed.

trickyParts: The stall is measured from the connection event, not from the first failed run: one hook run legitimately spends tens of seconds, because each JetStream call waits nats.MaxWait (10 s) and the caches are rewatched in sequence. The smoke shows it - the first WARN carried stall_ms=20007, two KV watch attempts of 10 s each.

A run that succeeds clears lastHookErr even when another connection event landed while it ran: without that, /healthz would name a fault that run had already repaired. The simplify pass found it; the stall itself restarts at the clock for the uncovered event.

The production-like smoke needs a NATS configuration whose permissions actually apply: a deny written beside its allow on one line is parsed into the allow list and the server applies no permissions at all (seen on /connz?auth=1), and KV_* is no NATS wildcard, since a wildcard is a whole token. The script writes one key per line and names the three KV streams in full.
bus.RepairGrace is exported because internal/kvwatch reads it (unrepairedDelay) and cmd/listener compares against it; it is the one bound both halves of an outage report at.
deviations: The plan's section 4 asked for the past-the-grace ERROR assertion in a new internal/bus test and in the updated restart_test.go. It is in restart_test.go's running-client case, which the plan also names; hook_stall_test.go's second test holds the reader (HookStall's stall and last error, which /healthz reads) rather than repeating the same log assertion.

The plan's negative control named a deny of $JS.API.CONSUMER.CREATE.KV_*.>; that subject matches nothing, since a NATS wildcard is a whole token. The smoke denies $JS.API.CONSUMER.CREATE.KV_envoy_interests.>, .KV_envoy_roles.> and .KV_envoy_sessions.> instead, which is the same band: STREAM.INFO, the pings and the durable keep working and only KV watch creation fails.
